title: Keep the analyzer working when source generation is suppressed

lines.text: > Note: When using Unity, dynamic code generation only works when targeting .NET Framework 4.x + mono runtime.
For all other Unity targets, AOT is required.
A `[MessagePackObject]` type can opt out of source generation with `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]`.
No formatter is generated for that type. It is serialized at run time by the dynamic resolvers, which use reflection, so such a type is not AOT-safe.
The analyzer still validates these types, because they are serialized at run time and must still have a valid contract:
- Keys are unique and all of the same kind ([MsgPack005](doc/analyzers/MsgPack005.md)).
- Members have types that are themselves serializable ([MsgPack003](doc/analyzers/MsgPack003.md)).
- Types are accessible to the resolver ([MsgPack012](doc/analyzers/MsgPack012.md)).

The analyzer does not report the partial-class requirement ([MsgPack011](doc/analyzers/MsgPack011.md)) or the AOT-only checks ([MsgPack016](doc/analyzers/MsgPack016.md) and [MsgPack017](doc/analyzers/MsgPack017.md)) for these types, because they only apply when a formatter is generated.
You can customize the generated source through properties on the `GeneratedMessagePackResolverAttribute`.

requirement.title: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true
requirement.intent: The analyzer must report its diagnostics for types that set SuppressSourceGeneration = true, as it did in version 3.1.0.

functional.text: The analyzer reports diagnostics for a [MessagePackObject] type with SuppressSourceGeneration = true.
The analyzer behaves for such types as it did in version 3.1.0, before the regression in 3.1.1.

nonFunctional.text: The analyzer must not crash on invalid input in a suppressed type; it reports the problem instead. (inferred)
Types that do not suppress source generation keep their current diagnostics. (inferred)

expectedBehaviours: Building a project with a [MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)] type that breaks an analyzer rule (for example a missing [Key] on a public member) shows the matching MsgPack diagnostic in the build output and the IDE.
Setting SuppressSourceGeneration = true no longer silences the analyzer: the type still gets analyzed even though no formatter is generated for it.
The source generator still writes no formatter for the suppressed type.
expectedTests: An analyzer test with a SuppressSourceGeneration = true type that is missing a Key attribute expects the matching MsgPack diagnostic at the member's location.
A generator snapshot test checks that a suppressed type still produces no formatter output while the diagnostics are reported.

expectedBehaviours: For suppressed types, the analyzer reports the same diagnostic IDs, severities and locations that version 3.1.0 reported for the same source.
Code that compiled cleanly with no diagnostics under 3.1.0 still compiles with no extra diagnostics for suppressed types.
expectedTests: A regression test reproduces the case from the issue and checks the diagnostics match the 3.1.0 results.
A test with a valid suppressed type checks that no diagnostics are reported.

expectedBehaviours: When a suppressed type has invalid input (for example duplicate keys, mixed key types, or a member type that cannot be resolved), the analyzer reports a diagnostic and does not throw.
The build log shows no AD0001 analyzer-exception warning and no generator crash warning for such types.
The rest of the compilation's diagnostics still get reported.
expectedTests: An analyzer test with a suppressed type that has duplicate or conflicting Key values expects the matching MsgPack diagnostic and no AD0001.
A test with a suppressed type whose member type is unresolvable checks that the analyzer finishes without an exception.

expectedBehaviours: Types without SuppressSourceGeneration, or with it set to false, show exactly the diagnostics they showed before the change.
Formatters and resolvers generated for non-suppressed types are unchanged, so the existing snapshot files under Resources still match.
No duplicate diagnostics show up for any type.
expectedTests: The existing analyzer and generator snapshot tests pass without any changes to their expected outputs.
A test with both a suppressed and a non-suppressed invalid type in one compilation checks that each diagnostic is reported exactly once.

story.what: In TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo, a property or field whose key kind does not match the other members is now skipped right after the DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys diagnostic is reported. Members are now added to the intMembers and stringMembers dictionaries only if their key is not already there, so a duplicate key gets the KeysMustBeUnique diagnostic instead of throwing. In MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.AnalyzeSymbol, the condition for reporting a formatter's inaccessible descriptor is flipped: it now fires only when the formatter is excluded from the source-generated resolver. The change also adds a README section, analyzer tests for SuppressSourceGeneration = true types, and execution tests for such a type.
story.why: Issue 2234 reports that the analyzer stopped working for types with SuppressSourceGeneration = true. With invalid input such as duplicate keys or mixed key kinds, the collector could throw (Dictionary.Add on a duplicate key, or intKey!.Value / stringKey! on a missing key) instead of reporting a diagnostic. The change makes the collector report these problems and keep going, so suppressed types are validated again, and it documents which diagnostics still apply to such types.

touches.note: The inaccessible-formatter condition changes from !ExcludeFromSourceGeneratedResolver to ExcludeFromSourceGeneratedResolver.
Skips members with a mismatched key kind and guards the dictionary adds against duplicate keys, for both properties and fields.
New analyzer tests for suppressed types and one non-suppressed duplicate-key case.
New execution tests: no generated formatter exists for the suppressed type, and the type round-trips through the dynamic resolver.

findings.title: Inaccessible-formatter check inverted for every formatter
findings.detail: In AnalyzeSymbol the condition changed from !formatter.ExcludeFromSourceGeneratedResolver to formatter.ExcludeFromSourceGeneratedResolver. The requirement does not ask for this, and it has nothing to do with SuppressSourceGeneration. After the change, MsgPack010 and MsgPack013 stop firing for inaccessible formatters that the generated resolver will silently leave out. They now fire for formatters the user deliberately excluded from the generated resolver. This changes diagnostics for types that do not suppress source generation, which breaks N2. It can also break builds that treat warnings as errors, and existing MsgPack010/013 tests should now fail.

findings.title: Mismatched-key members skip recursive collection, losing nested diagnostics
findings.detail: The new continue after DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys also skips the CollectCore call at the end of the member loop. Take a string-keyed type whose later member has an int key. Before, that member's type was still collected. Now the member's type is never analyzed, so MsgPack003 and other diagnostics for that type are no longer reported, which differs from 3.1.0 behaviour (F2). Applies to both the property path and the field path.

citations.quote: continue; // The key kind does not match the other members; the diagnostic is reported, so skip this member.

findings.title: Field with null string key can still crash the analyzer
findings.detail: In the field loop, if the first keyed member is a field with [Key((string)null)], searchFirst sets isIntKey to false. Execution then reaches the else branch, which calls stringMembers.ContainsKey(stringKey!) with a null key and throws ArgumentNullException. BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull is reported first but the analyzer still throws (AD0001). N1 requires that invalid input in a suppressed type is reported, not crashed on. The new guards here do not handle a null key.

findings.title: No tests for the field paths of the crash fixes
findings.detail: The new tests cover duplicate and mixed keys only on properties. The changed field-loop code has no test that runs it: the mixed-key continue, the guarded intMembers add and the guarded stringMembers add. A regression there would cause AD0001 again without any test failing.

findings.title: No test for unresolvable member type in a suppressed type
findings.detail: The expectation for N1 asks for a test that the analyzer finishes without an exception when a suppressed type has a member whose type cannot be resolved. No such test was added.

findings.title: No test for mixed suppressed and non-suppressed types in one compilation
findings.detail: N2 expects a test where a suppressed and a non-suppressed invalid type sit in the same compilation and each diagnostic is reported exactly once. The added tests each contain a single type.

refusals.reason: The new README section commits publicly to which diagnostics are reported (MsgPack003/004/005/012/015) and which are not (MsgPack011/016/017) for SuppressSourceGeneration types, which is a documented-behaviour contract for the maintainers to decide.
